title: A finite admissible coordinate cover over the original base
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There exist finitely many affine opens $U_a\subset X$, affine opens $V_a\subset Y$, and etale maps $e_a^0:U_a\to\mathbf A^d_{V_a}$ over $V_a$, with $f(U_a)\subset V_a$, whose inclusions $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow X$ cover $X$. Here affine space and etale maps have the meanings of [def-sbc-affine-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. The composite $e_a:U_a\to\mathbf A^d_{V_a}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y$ is separated etale of finite presentation, and $fj_a=p_de_a$. Each $j_a$ is a quasi-compact open immersion of finite type [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The schemes $U_a,V_a,\mathbf A^d_{V_a},\mathbf A^d_Y$ are Noetherian (they admit finite affine covers by spectra of rings with ascending chain condition on ideals), separated and finite type over $k$; in particular all chart maps meet the geometric hypotheses of finite-ring compact-support and sum-extension adjunctions. The empty cover is allowed for $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; finite-cover and separated finite-presentation admissibility elaborated in retained Step 13 of the exceptional-comparison proof

proof.text: The only ideals of the field $k$ are $0$ and $k$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (its one-point space is quasi-compact and its single affine chart has a Noetherian ring). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure maps of $X$ and $Y$: both schemes are Noetherian. Also [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] applies to these separated finite-type maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, giving quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $X$ and $Y$.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; Schemes Tags 01K4, 01KN, 01KU (qcqs over an affine base)

proof.text: For each $x\in X$, apply [lem-sc-standard-smooth-local-relative-dimension] to obtain affine opens $U_x=\operatorname{Spec}A_x\subseteq X$ and $V_x=\operatorname{Spec}R_x\subseteq Y$, with $x\in U_x$, $f(U_x)\subseteq V_x$, and induced ring map $R_x\to A_x$ standard smooth of relative dimension exactly $d$. By [lem-sc-standard-smooth-etale-polynomial-chart] choose an etale $R_x$-algebra map $\psi_x:R_x[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\to A_x$ whose restriction to constants is that induced ring map. Its map on spectra is etale, as that cited statement explicitly asserts. The affine-space description [def-sbc-affine-space] identifies its target with $\mathbf A^d_{V_x}$. Define $e_x^0$ by this map of spectra. Its composite with the projection has ring map $R_x\to A_x$; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square] identifies this composite, followed by $V_x\hookrightarrow Y$, with $f|_{U_x}$.

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space, proof (last d variables); Tags 01V7 and 02G1 for the prescribed relative dimension; Schemes Tag 01I1 for the affine square

proof.text: The opens $U_x$ cover $X$ because each contains its indexing point. By Step 1 and the definition [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], this open cover has a finite subcover $U_a$; retain each selected $V_a$ and $e_a^0$. If $X=\varnothing$, instead take the empty indexing set. This is just the finite-subcover clause of quasi-compactness and introduces no additional geometric assertion.

For every retained chart, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] shows that $U_a$ and $V_a$ are Noetherian, hence quasi-compact. Their inclusions $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow X$ and $v_a:V_a\hookrightarrow Y$ are open immersions by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Since $X,Y$ are quasi-separated by Step 1, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $j_a,v_a$ quasi-compact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes both inclusions of finite type. Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] makes them separated. Composing them with the structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, use [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] (1) and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e) to conclude that $U_a,V_a$ are separated and finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tags 01OW, 01OZ (open subschemes of Noetherian schemes); Schemes Tags 03GI, 01L7, 01KU; Morphisms Tags 01T2, 01T3

proof.text: For $S=Y$ and $S=V_a$, the projection $p_{d,S}:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ is affine: over every affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, its preimage is $\operatorname{Spec}R[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$, by [def-sbc-affine-space] and [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3), $p_{d,S}$ is separated and quasi-compact. It is locally of finite type directly from [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: the displayed ring is generated over $R$ by the $d$ variables, and this single affine open covers the preimage of $W$. Thus $p_{d,S}$ is of finite type. Composing with $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] (1) and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e) show that $\mathbf A^d_Y$ and $\mathbf A^d_{V_a}$ are separated and finite type over $k$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to these structure maps proves that both are Noetherian.

The restriction of $\mathbf A^d_Y$ over $V_a$ is $\mathbf A^d_{V_a}$, by [def-sbc-affine-space]. Thus $\rho_a:\mathbf A^d_{V_a}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y$ is the inclusion of the open inverse image $p_{d,Y}^{-1}(V_a)$, an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Set $e_a=\rho_a e_a^0$. The restriction identity $p_{d,Y}\rho_a=v_a p_{d,V_a}$ and Step 2 give $p_{d,Y}e_a=fj_a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1),(2), $\rho_a$ is etale and $e_a$ is etale. This constructs the maps over the original base $Y$, without changing that base.

source.place: Tags 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale); restriction of affine space to an open of its base

proof.text: Every target $\mathbf A^d_Y$ or $\mathbf A^d_{V_a}$ is quasi-separated by Step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. Each chart source $U_a$ is affine. Therefore the explicit affine-source clause of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1) applies to the etale maps $e_a$ and $e_a^0$ and makes both of finite presentation. In particular they are quasi-compact and locally of finite type: in the presentation of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables is generated by the images of those variables, so local finite presentation implies local finite type. Hence they are of finite type as well. Their composites with the target structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ equal the structure map of $U_a$, separated by Step 4. Cancellation [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] (b) makes both chart maps separated. All schemes and maps in the claimed charts now have the required Noetherian, separated and finite-type properties. When $d=0$, the polynomial algebra has no variables and $\mathbf A^0_S=S$ by [def-sbc-affine-space]; every preceding construction and finiteness argument still applies.

split_report.summary: Seven-step split using only existing DAG nodes. Construct fixed-dimension affine standard-smooth charts and their etale polynomial maps, take a finite subcover, and verify Noetherianity, separation, finite type and finite presentation. The open base restriction is composed into affine space over the original Y. Checked the empty scheme and relative dimension zero; no new nodes or statement correction.

Steps 4-5 check open subschemes Noetherian, qc inclusions via qcqs-permanence (1), qc open immersion of finite type, affine projection that is separated, qc and locally of finite type, and the compositions. Step 6 composes into A^d over the original base Y with p e_a = f j_a. Step 7 gets finite presentation from the affine-source clause, finite type, and separation by cancellation (b) against U_a over Spec k. These meet the hypotheses of the citer's chart nodes (chart-finite-ring-adjunction, chart-left-scalar-normalization, etale-sum-counit-scalar, open-exceptional-scalar-locality).
